headline: Validation design governs whether predictive claims survive held-out testing
label: Validation Design In Computational Biology
summary: Recent preprints evaluate predictions against held-out cohorts, source-context ranking, and identifiability checks rather than benchmark accuracy alone.
synthesis: The dominant thread in this set is that validation structure, rather than benchmark performance alone, is treated as the object of evaluation. Several items test whether a transfer claim holds under a specific design. The HNSCC Elastic Net is trained on GDSC cell lines and validated on TCGA-HNSC and GSE65858, and the source-selection study asks whether transcriptomic similarity ranks source contexts beyond tissue lineage for held-out drug responses. The endometrial study uses identifiability-aware models and simulations to separate temporal delay from amplitude loss, while ssGSEA3.0 replaces feature-label permutation with feature-level bootstrap resampling to address significance calibration. A single-cell reanalysis of 252,106 glioma cells examines whether response direction is coherent across malignant states. The COPD network-CNN and HNSCC excerpts report no accuracy figures, so predictive validity is not established there. The thread is not shared uniformly across all items.
